findings.issue: Depends on nitro ^3.0.261029-rc — the first v3 Release Candidate, published 2026-10-29 — and the caret range will silently pull in later RCs, whose channel has already carried breaking config changes.
findings.suggestion: Pin the exact RC version and add a comment, or track nitro releases and cut to v3 stable the moment it lands; the rest of the stack is stable so this is the only upgrade risk.

findings.issue: The whole runtime stack (SolidStart 2.0 stable 2026-08-04, 2.1.0 released 2026-10-22, router 1.0 realigned ~3 months ago) is only one quarter old.
findings.suggestion: Expected churn for a current-framework app; keep the migration guides handy and budget for patch updates, no action needed now.

findings.issue: The single experimental/RC integration (nitro vite plugin) is undocumented in-repo as to why it is used.
findings.suggestion: A one-line comment noting that nitro() provides the Node server output for SolidStart v2 would help future maintainers understand the only pre-stable link in the chain.

summary: The app targets the framework's current stable release (SolidStart 2 on Vite 8, router 1.0) and its application code uses only long-stable Solid APIs, with no experimental markers, flags or directives. The single pre-stable dependency is Nitro v3's first Release Candidate (published 2026-10-29), used as the server build plugin exactly as SolidStart v2's docs prescribe. That RC is fully contained in package.json and a five-line vite.config, so exposure is low and justified, with the main residual risk being automatic RC churn via the caret range.
